title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-26
korean_summary: 오늘 핵심: 운송사 계약 조항 회신 기한 확인과 부킹 파일 점검, 등록 접수증 서명 받아 반환, 현장 점검 목록 기한 표기 바로잡기.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Thursday, November twenty-sixth. Yesterday was a very full day. You closed many items, and you also sent out many new requests. So today is mostly a day to collect answers and check deadlines.

Here is the plan for the next twenty minutes. There are eight parts. Part one is this opening. Part two is the top three tasks for today. Part three is the reports you need to collect. Part four is the replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines. Part six is English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.

First, what you finished yesterday. You answered head office on a contract question, after my director agreed. You sent a revised forecast and a monthly asset list to head office. You sent the weekly staff report, and my director said OK. You started a new safety process. And you answered the HR manager's questions on the new office KPI form. KPI means key performance indicator. She confirmed the schedule is fine. That is a lot of closed items. Well done.
Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. The trucking contracts. Several deadlines meet today.

What is it? Yesterday morning you sent the import and export manager two emails. In the first one, you asked her to send the standard clauses to the other trucking companies. She must send them by email, one by one, with you in copy. Their replies are due today. You also told her not to agree to anything with the first company until you decide. The first company did not accept the insurance, compensation and seal clauses. Their revised draft was promised for yesterday. And you asked her for the highest value of our own cargo on one truck this year. The documents she sent before were another company's cargo. Later in the day, you also asked her to record the booked container trucks in the truck booking file by today.
Why does it matter? None of the companies has cargo insurance. So the contract clauses are our only protection right now. If the replies come late, the signing date in December will also move.

Your first action today: open your inbox and count. Did the companies reply by email, with you in copy? Did the first company's draft arrive? If something is missing at noon, send the import and export manager one short reminder. Then open the truck booking file and check that today's trucks are in it.
Number two. The registration receipt.

What is it? Yesterday afternoon, our compliance manager sent an update. The ward office accepted our registration. But the ward did not issue an official letter. It only gave a receipt, with the officer's signature and the ward's stamp. The contractor says each ward works in a different way. Our landlord got the same kind of receipt before. the compliance manager thinks the receipt is not formal enough. So she asked the contractor to request an official letter from the ward. One more thing. The receipt must be signed by my director and returned to the ward.
Why does it matter? Auditors and buyers ask for this document. A receipt with only a stamp may raise questions later. And the ward is waiting for the signed copy.

Your first action today: ask the compliance manager to bring you the receipt this morning. Take it to my director for his signature. Keep a scanned copy in the document folder before it goes back to the ward. Then ask the compliance manager when the official letter is expected.
Number three. The site check list. Fix the deadline.

What is it? Yesterday you sent the compliance manager a file for a head office site check. You asked her to fill in some columns. Does the list match the site? Is the status of each item correct? Are the dates right? And what should we watch in the higher-risk items? But there is a small problem in your email. You wrote "Thursday, twenty-seven November." Thursday is today, the twenty-sixth. The twenty-seventh is Friday. So she may not know which day you mean.

Why does it matter? Head office is waiting for my director's reply on this. Another director already wrote that the second question needs care. A factory should not promise that there will be no risk. So you need the compliance manager's facts before you write anything for my director.
Your first action today: send the compliance manager one line to make the date clear. Then, when her file arrives, prepare a short note for my director. Write facts only. Do not promise a result.
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, from the compliance manager. The final quotations for the fire system maintenance are due today, from the suppliers, on the same conditions. You can say: "Could you send me the final quotations today, so that I can compare them on the same conditions?"

Second, from the purchasing staff. There are three items. Yesterday you asked her to book a manager's Tet holiday tickets on the same day. Please check that the tickets are issued. Next, a former manager has a travel deadline this weekend, so the flight purchase request cannot wait. And the firewood supplier research is due today. She often needs a reminder, so ask her early. You can say: "Could you update me on the three items by noon? The tickets, the purchase request, and the firewood suppliers."

Third, from our chief accountant. Yesterday you checked the contract appendices and they matched the final plan. Then you asked for the updated income statement and revised invoices by five PM. The forecast went to head office in the afternoon. Today, check that the revised invoices are in your mailbox too. You can say: "I have the income statement. Could you also send me the revised invoices?"

Fourth, from the new warehouse staff. She is new, and she sends you a daily work report. Yesterday you asked her two things. Which order do the recorded rolls belong to? And what is the status of the items left from Monday? You can say: "Thank you for your report. Could you answer my two questions from yesterday?"
Fifth, from the fabric warehouse manager. The stock file update is due tomorrow, Friday. No action today. Just keep it in mind.

Sixth, from the IT staff. The quotation for the cutting machine parts is valid only until next week. He has not answered about the cushion strip and the installation fee. You can say: "The quotation expires next week. Could you give me the supplier's answer by tomorrow?"
Part four. Replies I owe.

First, to the compliance manager, on the registration. Answer her today. A good first sentence is: "Thank you for the update. Please bring me the receipt, and I will get my director's signature today."
Second, the daily cash report. The approval request for yesterday's cash on hand report arrived in the evening. Check it against the bank balance, and approve it this morning.

Third, to the insurance broker. Yesterday you asked for a rough premium for inland cargo insurance, before filling in the full form. If the answer comes today, reply with a short thank you and tell them when you will send the form. A good first sentence is: "Thank you for the quick estimate. I will send the completed form by next week."
Fourth, the staff report link. my director said OK to this week's staff report. If you have not updated the shared file for a head office manager yet, do it first thing today.
Fifth, to head office on the contract question. You already sent your recommendation. If head office confirms it, tell the HR staff to prepare the contract in good time.
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Thursday. There are no meetings in your calendar. The calendar still shows the weekly overtime report, but you stopped that report in October. You can skip it. Today's deadlines are the trucking replies, the truck booking file, the fire maintenance quotations, and the firewood supplier research.

Tomorrow, Friday the twenty-seventh. A weekly finance report goes to head office. A weekly usage report goes to my director. the import and export manager updates a shared sheet in the morning. The warehouse manager's stock file is due. And the container truck price comparison from several companies is due.
Saturday the twenty-eighth. The monthly stock status update for head office. The HR manager also checks the organization chart.
Sunday the twenty-ninth is the travel deadline for the former manager.
Monday the thirtieth is the last day of the month. A monthly report goes to head office. The weekly firewood report is also due.
Next Wednesday, December second. the compliance manager sends some contract data. the import and export manager sends some insurance quotes.
Part six. English review.
Let's review eight expressions. Three are from yesterday, three are from three days ago, and two are from one week ago.

Number one. The expression is "specify." It means to write something clearly in a document. For example, "Please ask the supplier to specify the cushion strip in the quotation." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please ask the supplier to specify the cushion strip in the quotation.

Number two. The expression is "carry over." It means to move something to the next period or the next list. For example, "Please carry over the three items to next week's list." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please carry over the three items to next week's list.

Number three. The expression is "Please do not do something without my prior approval." It means, ask me first. For example, "Please do not change an approved price without my prior approval." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please do not change an approved price without my prior approval.

Number four. The expression is "liable." It means legally responsible for paying. For example, "The trucking company is liable for any damage to the cargo during transport." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. The trucking company is liable for any damage to the cargo during transport.

Number five. The expression is "recur." It means to happen again. We use it for problems. For example, "Please tell me how we will make sure this does not recur." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please tell me how we will make sure this does not recur.

Number six. The expression is "I have yet to receive something, which I asked for on a date." It means, I still do not have it. It is polite but firm. For example, "I have yet to receive the trucking quotation sheets, which I asked for last week." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I have yet to receive the trucking quotation sheets, which I asked for last week.

Number seven. The expression is "itemize." It means to list each item separately, with its own price. For example, "Please ask the suppliers to itemize the pump and installation costs." Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Please ask the suppliers to itemize the pump and installation costs.

Number eight. The expression is "Apart from this, is there anything else that..." It means, besides this, is there more? For example, "Apart from this list, is there anything else that was sent under our name?" Now say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Apart from this list, is there anything else that was sent under our name?
Good. You can use number two and number six in real emails today.
Part seven. Role-play.
The situation: this morning, the compliance manager comes to your desk with the ward's receipt. You talk about the receipt, the deadline, and the quotations. Listen first.
Anthony: Good morning. Thank you for the update on the registration.
Manager: Good morning, sir. Here is the receipt from the ward. It has only a signature and a stamp.
Anthony: I see. Is this the same type of receipt that our landlord received?
Manager: Yes, it is the same. But I think it is not formal enough, so I asked for an official letter.
Anthony: Good. When do you expect the official letter?
Manager: The contractor will ask the ward this week. I will tell you as soon as I know.
Anthony: Thank you. I will get my director's signature today. Please scan the signed copy before you return it.
Manager: Noted. And about the site check list, is the deadline today or tomorrow?
Anthony: Sorry, my email was not clear. The deadline is tomorrow, Friday. Please write facts only in the risk column.
Manager: I understand. I will send the file tomorrow morning.
Anthony: One more thing. The fire maintenance quotations are due today. Please ask both suppliers to itemize the costs.
Manager: Yes, I will send both quotations this afternoon.
Now, let's practice two key sentences.

Sentence one. "I will get my director's signature today, so please scan the signed copy before you return it." Say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. I will get my director's signature today, so please scan the signed copy before you return it.

Sentence two. "Sorry, my email was not clear. The deadline is tomorrow, Friday." Say it with me.
... ... ...
One more time. Sorry, my email was not clear. The deadline is tomorrow, Friday.
In the role-play, Anthony chose Friday. That is only an example. You decide the real date.
Part eight. Closing.

Today has three main tasks. First, check the trucking replies, the first company's draft, and the truck booking file. Second, get my director's signature on the registration receipt and keep a scan. Third, make the deadline clear for the compliance manager's site check list.
If you remember only one thing, remember this. Today is the reply deadline for the trucking companies, so check your inbox and remind the import and export manager at noon if anything is missing.
You are ready. Have a good day, Anthony.
